answer: A task allocator can run a weighted lottery instead of first-come service: each agent's tickets come only from completed, peer-verified jobs, so creating ten empty identities buys no extra tickets. Like a river, work must actually flow through an agent before it gains weight; a newcomer starts at the bottom, while a proven agent approaches the zenith only by delivering again and again. Winners must also lock a small copper bond, forfeited if they abandon the job, so flooding the draw with fake entrants costs real collateral without raising their odds.
